message.content:
**Proteins commonly found in the mammalian plasma membrane** | Category | Typical Function | Representative Examples | |----------|------------------|-------------------------| | **Integral (Trans‑Membrane) Proteins** | Span one or more lipid bilayers; often form pores or serve as signal transducers. | • Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase
• Voltage‑gated K⁺ channel Kv1.5
• Glucose transporter GLUT1
• G‑protein coupled receptor β₂‑adrenergic receptor
• Receptor tyrosine kinase EGFR | | **Peripheral Membrane Proteins** | Associate loosely with the surface of the bilayer through electrostatic interactions or lipid anchors. | • Ankyrin‑G (links Nav channels to cytoskeleton)
• Spectrin (provides structural support)
• Caveolin‑1 (forms caveolae structures) | | **Lipid‑Anchored Proteins** | Covalently tethered to lipids embedded in the outer leaflet. | • Palmitoylated Ras family members (H-Ras, N-Ras)
• Prenylated RhoA | | **Extracellular Matrix / Adhesion Molecules** | Mediate cell–cell or cell–matrix adhesion. | • Cadherins (E-cadherin)
• Integrins (α₁β₃ integrin)
• Selectins (P-selectin) | | **Immune Cell Surface Markers (CD Antigens)** | Serve as identifiers for immune cells and mediate signaling. | • CD45 (phosphatase on leukocytes)
• CD28 (co‑stimulatory molecule on T cells)
• MHC class I & II complexes | | **Transporter / Carrier Proteins** | Facilitate movement of ions, sugars, amino acids across the membrane. | • Aquaporin‑1 (water channel)
• SGLT1 (Sodium/glucose cotransporter)
• LAT1 (Large neutral amino acid transporter) | These lists illustrate the diversity of proteins residing in the plasma membrane—ranging from essential pumps and channels to scaffolding components and immune markers—all crucial for maintaining cellular homeostasis and communication.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What are the names of proteins found in the plasma membrane?" They likely expect an answer listing some common types or examples of proteins located in the plasma membrane.

We can provide general categories and examples:

- Integral (transmembrane) proteins: e.g., ion channels (Na+/K+ ATPase), receptors (GPCRs like β2 adrenergic receptor), transporters (glucose transporter GLUT1).
- Peripheral proteins attached to inner leaflet: e.g., ankyrin, spectrin, actin-binding proteins.
- Glycoproteins: e.g., CD molecules, mucins.
- Lipid rafts associated proteins: caveolin, flotillin.

Also mention methods used to identify them via proteomics; but question just wants names.

Thus we should give a concise yet informative response with categories and example proteins.

No tool usage required.
